title: II–III. Penal condition: eternal curse or paternal chastisement; curse remains on unbelievers
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): it remains only toward those who do not receive ye testimony belonging toward Christ. Of eternal curse plus death we treated above in Book II chapter 15; insofar as paradise was a figure belonging toward ye heavenly dwelling — a type belonging toward this was ye ejection out from paradise. those not receiving Christ, ye truth) their portion stands as in ye lake where fire plus sulphur burn, that same which stands as ye second death — but toward ye fearful plus unbelieving plus abominable plus murderers plus fornicators plus sorcerers plus idolaters plus all liars (that is. Revelation 21:8: but ye wrath belonging toward God remains upon him — but whoever does not assent to ye Son will not see life. John 3:36: But whoever does not believe will be condemned. The matter stands as clear in Mark 16:16: ye guilt belonging toward ye human race having been transferred onto Christ, remains toward those who do not receive Him — eternal curse stands as that same which. III. The penal condition therefore stands as belonging toward eternal curse or belonging toward paternal chastisement. II.
pass_b_english: II. The penal condition therefore is of eternal curse or of paternal chastisement. III. Eternal curse is that which, the guilt of the human race having been transferred onto Christ, remains for those who do not receive Him. The matter is clear in Mark 16:16: But whoever does not believe will be condemned. John 3:36: But whoever does not assent to the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him. Revelation 21:8: But for the fearful and unbelieving and abominable and murderers and fornicators and sorcerers and idolaters and all liars (that is, those not receiving Christ, the truth) their portion is in the lake where fire and sulphur burn, which is the second death. A type of this was the ejection from paradise, insofar as paradise was a figure of the heavenly dwelling. Of eternal curse and death we treated above in Book II chapter 15; it remains only for those who do not receive the testimony of Christ.
source_text: II. Poenalis conditio igitur est maledictionis aeternae aut castigationis paternae. III. Maledictio aeterna est, quae propter culpam humani generis in Christum translata, eos manet qui hunc non recipiunt. Res clara est Marc. 16:16: Qui vero non crediderit, condemnabitur. Ioh. 3:36: Qui vero non assentitur Filio, non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum. Apoc. 21:8: Formidolosis autem et incredulis et exsecrabilibus et homicidis et scortatoribus et veneficis et idololatris et omnibus mendacibus (id est, Christum, veritatem non recipientibus) portio est in stagno ubi ardet ignis et sulphur, quod est mors secunda. Huius typus fuit eiectio e paradiso, quatenus paradisus fuit caelestis domicilii figura. De maledictione vero et morte aeterna supra egimus lib. 2 cap. XV, quae eos duntaxat manet qui testimonium Christi non recipiunt.
